purpose: Test whether a deployment-relevant receptor-opening and chemistry-series routing problem develops a reproducible gap between global optimization and strong classical search as the real PPARG MD receptor pool grows.

chemistry_series_freeze.eligible_ligands: 80 active ligands only; all 80 decoys remain a global exposure panel
chemistry_series_freeze.fingerprint: RDKit Morgan radius 2, 2048 bits, chirality disabled
chemistry_series_freeze.clustering: deterministic complete-linkage hierarchy over ligand_id-sorted fingerprints; selected before solver execution because it had the smallest maximum cluster at every frozen cluster count among single, complete, average, and weighted linkage

objective.series_assignment: each active chemical series is routed to exactly one pair of opened receptors
objective.pair_hit_rule: union: a ligand is hit when either receptor ranks it in the seed-specific top 10 percent
objective.global_objective: active-count-weighted mean pair-series utility over all chemical series
objective.reason_for_active_count_weighting: routing value scales with the number of active ligands represented and does not allow singleton clusters to dominate the objective

nested_receptor_rule: For an R-receptor scale, retain temporal_maximin_rank < R/8 from each of the eight pre-existing MD starts. This uses no docking score or ligand label.

classical_baselines.adaptive_escalation_rule: run preliminary baselines first; if and only if a certified MILP optimum exceeds the preliminary best by at least 1 percent, run the full confirmation baselines before adjudication

stop_rule: If no scale has a certified classical gap, do not encode Stage95 for quantum hardware and do not tune this objective on the same PPARG matrix.
